--- title: "[Graph.edge_betweenness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate betweenness centrality scores for all edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L27669-L27805){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.edge_betweenness_centrality( normalized=True, weighted=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Edge betweenness centrality](/assets/graphs/edge-betweenness-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph with each edge drawn thicker the more shortest paths run through it. The bridge E-F, which every path from the triangles to the tail must cross, is thickest and in accent at 0.48, ahead of C-E at 0.36 and F-G at 0.29; the triangle edges A-B and C-D carry the least, 0.07." width="100%"} Edge betweenness centrality measures how many shortest paths run through each edge. For every pair of nodes, each shortest path between them contributes to the edges it uses; when a pair has several shortest paths, each one counts for an equal share. Edges with high scores carry a lot of the graph's traffic: they are bridges between clusters, bottlenecks, and the first links to fail or congest. This is the edge counterpart of `betweenness_centrality()`, and it is the quantity that the Girvan-Newman method (`cmty_edge_btwns()`, `cmty_girvan_newman()`) removes edges by to split a graph into communities. Use it on its own to: - find the links whose loss would most lengthen paths in a network - spot inter-community edges before running community detection - weight or prune edges by how structurally important they are Parallel edges are separate routes and split their shared paths between them; self-loops score `0`. On a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`) shortest paths minimize total edge weight (Dijkstra's algorithm), so only the cheapest parallel edges carry paths; on an unweighted graph they minimize hops. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), divide scores by `n * (n - 1)`, the number of ordered node pairs, so they fall in `[0, 1]`. If `False`, return raw path counts (halved for undirected graphs so that each unordered pair is counted once). Both match NetworkX's `edge_betweenness_centrality()`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to measure distances by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph: weights are used on a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`) and hop counts otherwise, the same rule `shortest_path()` uses. Pass `True` or `False` to override. Edges without a weight count as `1.0`; weights must be non-negative. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the edge attribute to store the scores in. If `None` (default), automatically uses `"edge_betweenness_centrality"`. Overwrites the attribute if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as an edge attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping edge IDs to betweenness scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles joined by a single edge: every path between the triangles must cross the bridge, so it has by far the highest score: ::: {#dadfd6e1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) .add_edge("C", "D") # the bridge .add_edges([("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) scores = graph.edge_betweenness_centrality(return_dict=True) label = graph.get_label_from_id { "-".join(label(n) for n in graph.get_node_ids_by_edge_id(eid)): round(s, 3) for eid, s in sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]) } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'C-D': 0.6, 'F-D': 0.267, 'C-A': 0.267, 'B-C': 0.267, 'D-E': 0.267, 'E-F': 0.067, 'A-B': 0.067} ``` ::: ::: With `normalized=False` the scores are path counts. The bridge lies on the shortest path of all `3 * 3 = 9` pairs that have one node in each triangle, plus none of the within-triangle pairs: ::: {#5c103e43 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} raw = graph.edge_betweenness_centrality(normalized=False, return_dict=True) max(raw.values()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 9.0 ``` ::: ::: Without `return_dict=`, the scores are stored on the edges, where they can be used to select or filter edges. The top row is the bridge, between node IDs 3 (`C`) and 4 (`D`): ::: {#4d8a685d .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.edge_betweenness_centrality(attr_name="ebc") graph.get_edge_df().select(["source", "target", "ebc"]).sort("ebc", descending=True).head(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
